name: Ouroboros Executive Division Poplin
description:
The standard dress shirt issued to Ouroboros Corponation's mid-to-upper management tier, cut from a wrinkle-resistant poplin weave that maintains its crispness through a fourteen-hour shift without ironing. The collar is a semi-spread construction with collar stays sewn directly into the fabric — they cannot be removed. French placket, mitered cuffs, a subtle geometric pattern woven into the white-on-white fabric that's only visible at certain angles of light. The Ouroboros serpent logo appears in embossed thread on the left cuff, small and tasteful.

The shirt comes in three colorways — white, pale grey, and a blue-grey that Ouroboros internal documentation calls 'Meridian Blue.' There is no off-the-rack version of this shirt; it is issued, not purchased, and the issuance is tracked. Wearing one outside of Ouroboros facilities without authorization is technically a breach of employment contract. Most people don't know that. The shirt fits well because Ouroboros took body scans during onboarding.
what_it_says: You work for Ouroboros, and you are in a position where Ouroboros has decided you should look like it. Whether that's a point of pride or a collar depends entirely on how you feel about your employer.
worn_by: anyone trying to pass as Ouroboros personnel
story_hooks: The collar stays in the shirt contain a passive RFID chip that logs the wearer's location whenever they pass an Ouroboros sensor node — the company maps its employees' movements more precisely than anyone realizes.

A character acquires one of these shirts and uses it to bluff their way into an Ouroboros facility, only to discover that the shirt itself broadcasts a low-level ID signal that the building's security reads on entry.

An Ouroboros mid-manager keeps wearing their issued shirt after being quietly let go — technically illegal, but they haven't been approached yet, and they're not sure if that's because nobody noticed or because someone is watching to see what they do next.
